To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NOA is richly immunostained by both CaBP and PV.
CaBP and PV are expressed in different proportions in the NOA and that their distribution patterns differ from one subdivision to another.
the nucleus olfactorious anterior is a complex structure that shows a heterogeneous distribution of calbindin and parvalbumine immunoreactivities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of CaBP and PV immunoreactivity in NOA, a nucleus which is involved in the olfactory system.
the distribution of the CaBP and PV immunoreactivities in NOA, and with their coexistence in the different neuronal populations of this nucleus.
the distribution of CaBP and PV in the NOA of the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaBP and PV immunoreactivity in NOA are not restricted to any one subdivision and that both proteins are expressed by a variety of neurons with different dendritic patterns.
the NOA has a complex organization, with different subdivisions, each one having a particular distribution for CaBP- and/or PV-immunoreactive neurons.

NOA is an olfactory-related structure, with the following characteristics: 1) it is a heterogeneous structure in terms of CaBP and PV distribution; 2) CaBP is the most abundant protein in NOA; 3) PV is less abundant than CaBP; and 4) the pars medialis is the only area in the NOA that shows a high PV immunostaining.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the distribution of CaBP- and/or PV-immunoreactive elements in the rat NOA is heterogeneous and the NOA is a complex structure, where different types of neurons are present, with different immunoreactivities.
CaBP and PV are differentially distributed in the NOA, with CaBP immunoreactivity being more abundant than the PV one.
CaBP- and/or PV-immunoreactivity was found throughout the NOA, but the distribution was not homogeneous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution patterns of both CaBP and PV in the NOA are similar to those found in other brain structures, but the distribution of CaBP in the NOAe and pars medialis is unique.
the distribution of CaBP and PV in the NOA is not uniform, and that the subdivisions of this nucleus show a differential expression of CaBP and a lack of PV.

the NOA is a heterogeneous structure, with different distributions of CaBP- and CaBP- and/or PV-positive neurons and fibres, which could indicate different functions for the different subdivisions of this nucleus.
